newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Bangui army dissidents vow to keep arms deadline.
newsitem.headline: Bangui army dissidents vow to keep arms deadline.

text.p: Dissident soldiers in the Central African Republic capital Bangui said on Wednesday that they would honour a pledge to return all heavy weapons under a four-day truce with African peacekeepers.
"What is certain is that we will hand over all the heavy weapons that are in our possession," spokesman Lieutenant Parfait Mbay told Radio France International.

With the truce expiring at 1900 GMT on Wednesday, monitors said the dissidents had handed in some mortars, but Mbay said they still had to establish how many were in their possession as some had possibly been thrown in the nearby River Oubangui.

The dissidents, a minority of whom had not returned to their units under a January peace deal to end three army mutinies in under a year, agreed to hand over their heavy weapons to former colonial power France's ambassador in Bangui.
Mali's widely respected former military leader, Amadou Toumani Toure, has been trying to extend the truce and set the January peace deal, which he brokered, back on track.
A week of clashes between former mutineers and African peacekeepers followed a June 20 incident. The Red Cross says about 100 people, mostly civilians, died in the fighting.
Relief workers say up to 60,000 people fled their homes for the relative safety of the countryside. Some have returned.

Mutinies in April and May 1996 began as pay protests but evolved into a bid to topple President Ange-Felix Patasse, a civilian from the north, elected in 1993. A third mutiny began in November and degenerated into ethnic bloodshed.
French troops intervened to halt that fighting and then handed over the peacekeepers under the January deal.
